subject: Core: expose catalog labels on the loaded table via SupportsLabels (#18046)
body:
* Core: expose labels on the loaded table via SupportsLabels

Builds on the labels read-path serde: make the catalog-provided labels from
the load response reachable by consumers.

- New SupportsLabels mixin interface (mirroring SupportsDistributedScanPlanning)
  with a single labels() accessor.
- BaseTable implements SupportsLabels via a new constructor that carries an
  optional Labels; existing constructors default to an empty instance. The field
  is transient and not copied into SerializableTable, so labels are ephemeral
  catalog enrichment and are not preserved across table serialization.
- RESTSessionCatalog populates labels from the load response for both the plain
  BaseTable and the server-side scan-planning RESTTable paths, across loadTable,
  registerTable, and createTable.

* Core: address review comments on the labels table PR

- Rename TestBaseTableLabels to TestLabelsOnBaseTable, drop a redundant comment,
  and assert the field-label contents (field id + labels), not just the count.
- Implement SupportsLabels on SerializableTable, returning Labels.EMPTY: labels
  are driver-side catalog enrichment and are not carried across serialization.

Co-authored-by: Isaac <no-reply@databricks.com>

* Core: address labels review feedback on SerializableTable and BaseTable

- Drop SupportsLabels from SerializableTable. Labels are transient catalog
  enrichment that is intentionally not shipped to executors, and the only
  consumer already guards with instanceof, so behavior is unchanged; a
  real label-carrying implementation stays additive if ever needed.
- Broaden the BaseTable#labels() null comment: the transient field is null
  after any deserialization that bypasses writeReplace(), not only Kryo.
- Make the TestLabelsOnBaseTable test methods package-private.

Co-authored-by: Isaac <no-reply@databricks.com>

* Core: add a RESTCatalog test for catalog labels on the loaded table

Loads a table through RESTCatalog backed by an adapter that returns
object- and field-level labels on the load-table response, and asserts
they are surfaced through SupportsLabels#labels().

subject: Core: Project tracked-file partitions onto the resolved spec (#18108)
body:
TrackedFileAdapters exposed the manifest's union-type partition tuple
unchanged while reporting the file's own spec ID. Residual evaluation and
partition-constant injection read the tuple by the spec's field ordinals, so
on partition-evolved tables a later spec's field (at a different position in
the union than in its own spec) was read from the wrong slot, silently
dropping rows or injecting null partition constants.

Project each file's partition onto its resolved spec's partition type before
exposing it, so partition() is always in the file's own spec order.

Co-authored-by: Isaac <no-reply@databricks.com>

subject: Core: Avoid redundant SplitScanTask wrapper for files that fit in a single split (#18002)
body:
* Core: Avoid redundant split wrapper for files smaller than target split size

BaseContentScanTask.split() wraps every splittable file in a SplitScanTask
even when the file already fits within a single split (length <= targetSplitSize).
For tables with many small files this allocates one redundant 1:1 wrapper
per data file during scan planning, adding Spark driver heap pressure.

Short-circuit that case: when a file fits in a single split, return the
task itself instead of constructing an iterator that would only ever
produce a single, functionally-identical wrapper.

Also make IcebergSourceSplit.splitId() class-agnostic so the split
identity is stable whether the underlying task is a BaseFileScanTask or
a SplitScanTask. Previously splitId embedded the concrete task class name
via MoreObjects.toStringHelper(fileScanTask), so the serialization
round-trip was not type-preserving (ScanTaskParser.fromJson always
returns a SplitScanTask), breaking TestIcebergEnumeratorStateSerializer.
Use a fixed label so splitId no longer depends on the runtime task type.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

subject: Spark: Use merge append by default for streaming writes (#18332)
body:
Spark 3.5, 4.0, 4.1, 4.2: Use merge append by default for streaming writes

Flip the default of the `use-merge-append-for-streaming` write option from
false to true, so streaming appends merge manifests on commit instead of
accumulating a small manifest per commit.

The option was added in 1.12 (#17347, #17403) defaulting to fast append to
give users a release to adjust in case anything relied on the one-manifest-
per-commit behavior. Now that 1.12 has shipped, flip the default for 1.13.

Fast append remains available by setting the option to false.

subject: Core: Bound Idempotency-Key retries to the advertised key lifetime (#18070)
body:
Auto-retrying a keyed mutation could previously fire after the server's advertised Idempotency-Key lifetime elapsed, at which point the server no longer dedupes the key and could apply the mutation twice. This records when a request is first sent (in HTTPClient.execute) and, for requests carrying an Idempotency-Key, declines a retry once the elapsed time since the first attempt plus the next retry interval would reach the advertised lifetime. The lifetime from GET /v1/config is plumbed through the client properties into ExponentialHttpRequestRetryStrategy; a non-positive window declines all keyed retries, while an absent or unparseable one leaves the bound disabled. The check applies to the response and network-exception retry paths; non-keyed and idempotent requests are unaffected.

Per Yufei's review, the check compares against the upper bound of the next retry interval (Retry-After verbatim, or exponential backoff plus its maximum jitter) rather than a freshly sampled value, so a retry the check permits cannot then sleep longer than checked and overshoot the window.

subject: Aliyun: Default random port for OSS mock server (#18249)
body:
AliyunOSSMock defaulted to the fixed port 9393, so running the aliyun
tests with more than one test fork made concurrent JVMs fight over the
same port. With -DtestParallelism=8, five of the eight test classes in
the module failed in beforeAll with "Can't start OSS Mock".

Default server.port to 0 and read the actual port back off the started
server, the same approach used in #6895 and #6959. An explicitly
configured server.port is still honoured.

Two related fork-safety problems in the same path:

- The BindException cause was discarded when wrapping the failure, which
  is why the collision surfaced as a bare "Can't start OSS Mock" with no
  indication that a port was at fault.
- The mock's store directory was named with System.currentTimeMillis(),
  so two forks starting in the same millisecond shared a store and
  deleted each other's objects during bucket teardown. Use a UUID.
